messages.body_plain:
Hi Alex,

Copying the mailing list as I think this is generally helpful.

Great! I've added libboost-dev to our renjin-package-builder VM image, but it looks like the version that ships with Ubuntu 14, which the build servers are running, has an older version of Boost:
http://packages.renjin.org/package/org.renjin.cran/dplyr/0.5.0/build/190

I get the same results you do my laptop with Ubuntu 16.

It also looks like the output of dplyr's native sources include an inline assembly node, which I hadn't encountered before. I've added <https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/commit/0b6ebc951d5b2f4cc9960c8bf88992f71a273565> it to the AST definition as well as stub to just throw an Exception at runtime. We can see later if it's critical to the package or not and then how to handle it.

After fixing this, there appear to be a number of problems compilingon Renjin's side. I fixed a few but I didn't have time to go through them all. The branch is here:
https://github.com/bedatadriven/renjin/tree/wip-dplyr

The next thing to fix is something called offset types, which I gather is used by GCC to represent C pointers-to-members.... Will require some digging to figure just what the heck this is, but should be reasonable to implement. Let me know if you get stuck!

Best,
Alex

[ERROR] Failed to execute goal org.renjin:renjin-maven-plugin:0.9.0-SNAPSHOT:gnur-compile (compile) on project dplyr: Compilation of GNU R sources failed: Failed to parse gimple file /home/ubuntu/renjin2/dplyr_0.5.0-b189/src/dplyr.gimple: Could not resolve type id 'gimple_asm' into a subtype of [simple type, class org.renjin.gcc.gimple.statement.GimpleStatement]

-------------

Thank you,

Alex

I'm working on getting the build working in latest master / VM and running into some issues - it seems like the build is passing elsewhere so I'm not sure what is causing the failures.

A few Integration Tests are failing from the 'tests' module:
https://github.com/alszeb/renjin/pull/1/commits/79b0b55c65242a53d3a34f84dfba1dba57a58f8f

it looks like 'micro' tests with the eigan function as well as a micro test with a %*% operator are failing.  I commit the commented-out-failing-tests as well as the failure logs for each of those types of cases at the above link. I tried installing `rcppeigan` and  `r-cran-ccpeigan` to the VM although neither of these seemed to help (note that my VM was in a dirty state at the time).

Once those tests are commented out, the build proceeds and I get the following failure:
[ERROR] Failed to execute goal org.renjin:renjin-maven-plugin:0.9.0-SNAPSHOT:gnur-compile (build) on project cran.dot.package: Compilation of GNU R sources failed: Cannot run program "make" (in directory "/home/ubuntu/renjin/test-packages/cran.dot.package/src"): error=2, No such file or directory -> [Help 1]

I want to figure out if its something with my environment or an issue with the VM - has anyone build renjin on a fresh vagrant up of the VM?

Any ideas on what to check out next?

Thank you,
Alex S.

messages.body_plain:
As more of my experimentation with using Renjin in my software I developed a prototype of a code studio based on JavaFX.  This combines some of my existing code with some from the Renjin studio (based on Swing).  Currently the GUI has an area for code editing, a console and a plot region. The console includes command completion (hit the Tab key).  Using this has a dependency on my experimental graphics for Renjin:

https://github.com/brucejohnson/jfxplot

StudioFX is available on github at:

https://github.com/brucejohnson/studiofx

This is very much a prototype and duplicates some code (like REPL.java) from Renjin.

cheers,

Bruce

messages.subject: Next week at UseR!
messages.body_plain:
Hi Everyone,

Myself, Maarten-Jan and Parham are all very excited to be attending UseR! next week in Brussels. Hope to see a few of you there!

Just want to highlight two events during the conference:

On Wednesday, we're co-hosting the RIOT: the 3rd Workshop on R Implementation, Optimization and Tooling, parallel to the conference:
https://riotworkshop.github.io/

If you're interested in the technical details behind R and Renjin, this is an amazing event. Developers from R Core, pQR, TERR, are all speaking, and Parham is making his RIOT debut with a presentation on JIT-compiling S4.

On Thursday, at 1:30, I'll presenting the new "renjin" package for GNU R, which allows you to load Renjin in GNU R and offload part of your workload to Renjin's compiler.

http://sched.co/AxqS

Please drop a line here or to me (al...@bedatadriven.com) if want to meet up at some other time to talk Renjin!

All the best,
Alex
